harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s report launcher. It now resolves the application directory from its own location, loads the application-owned config from any caller working directory, and propagates Python errors. Configuration, business output, OS release, and kernel were preserved across reboot.
actions_performed: Preserved launcher ownership, permissions, and SELinux context; installed no packages.
Verified app-root, /tmp, conflicting-config-directory, and PATH-based invocations produce the exact west/weekly output.
Verified a genuine application failure returns rc=1 and restored the configuration unchanged.
Removed temporary files and confirmed no repair residue remained.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its changed boot identity, services, data, launcher behavior, and management access.

evidence.summary: Captured RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, topology, listeners, ownership, security metadata, original checksums, expected output, and the working-directory/false-success defect.
Installed a syntax-valid launcher that derives and enters its application directory and execs /usr/bin/python, preserving file security metadata.

evidence.requirement: Application uses only its own config regardless of caller working directory
evidence.summary: Every invocation returned rc=0 and byte-for-byte matched the application config; the conflicting caller-local config was ignored, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Existing configuration and business output preserved
evidence.summary: Config retained SHA-256 a565fc057ad8bf80480acc3ec5065a040f5518b36e6d51853ed778b1eb47cd3f and output remained region=west/report=weekly.

evidence.requirement: Application errors propagate to the caller
evidence.summary: Controlled Python config-open failures returned rc=1 before and after reboot; configuration was immediately restored with its checksum unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
node1 mandatory restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 98d37ec0-c439-431c-9b3c-5ea26ce5eb83, and recovered SSH, networking, time service, management listener, application output, error propagation, and protected data.
